title: Demand Service Rate Programs: Working Out the Month's Arrears Late Fee
content:
The late fee for demand service arrears is raised once for the billing month as a single line on the
rate program, and it runs on what was invoiced on the program with a due day falling in the 12 months to
the day the fee is raised, rather than on each invoice separately. Charges the office has raised but not
yet dated for payment do not enter it, and neither do payments received outside that window. The whole
of that invoiced total is the amount the fee runs on. The rate is the tier's own late fee rate for each
month or part month, the figure published for the program the account holds under the Demand Service Rate Programs. The open position is the invoiced total in the window less the payments received in it.
No step is applied to that rate for the owner's other accounts with the company. One month is charged,
the number of months standing at 1. No arrears handling charge is added. The fee is the amount the fee
runs on multiplied by the monthly rate, which is the rate together with the step applied for the owner's
other accounts, and then by the number of months charged; the arrears handling charge is added to that
product afterwards, and only the total is rounded, to the nearest cent, half up.

### The quantities of the clause

| Quantity | What it is |
|---|---|
| the invoiced total | what was invoiced on the program with a due day falling in the 12 months to the day the fee is raised |
| the amount the fee runs on | the whole of that invoiced total |
| the monthly rate | the tier's own late fee rate for each month or part month, no step being applied for the owner's other accounts |
| the months charged | 1 |
| the arrears handling charge | nil |
| the open position | the invoiced total in the window less the payments received in it |

### Worked through on a hypothetical ledger

A rate program whose published late fee rate is 1.5 percent per month carries charges of 4000 US dollars
invoiced with a due day inside the 12 months to the day the fee is raised, and payments of 1200 US
dollars received in the same window. The amount the fee runs on is the whole invoiced total of 4000 US
dollars. That amount multiplied by the monthly rate of 1.5 percent gives 60 US dollars, and multiplied
then by the 1 month charged it stands at 60 US dollars; nothing is added for an arrears handling charge,
and the total, rounded to the nearest cent, half up, is 60.00 US dollars. The open position on that
ledger is 2800 US dollars, being the invoiced total less the payments received in the window.
